fichas.title: Construction drawing symbols: windows
fichas.summary: Plan symbols show window openings set in wall reveals, including inward- and outward-opening single and double windows, box windows, sash windows, and sliding windows. The left side of a window drawing is shown with a wall niche and the right side without.
uses: Represent window types and opening direction in construction drawings

fichas.title: Construction drawing symbols: doors and folding partition
fichas.summary: Plan symbols identify single- and double-leaf doors, pivoting and sliding doors, revolving doors, threshold conditions, a lifting sliding mechanism, and a folding partition. The accompanying note says revolving doors can replace wind lobbies and that their leaves can be folded aside at peak times.
uses: Represent door type, operation, and threshold conditions in construction drawings
Show revolving-door alternatives to wind lobbies

fichas.title: Construction drawing symbols: stairs
fichas.summary: Stairwell plan symbols illustrate stairs with one flight and two flights across cellar, ground-floor, upper-floor, and attic levels. The notes instruct that stair sections on floor plans are shown at about one-third storey height or 1 m above floor level, with steps numbered continuously from ±0.000; steps below that level receive a minus sign, and the centre-line starts with a circle and ends with an arrow.
uses: Represent stair flights and direction in floor plans
Number stair steps continuously across levels
Indicate stair section location on floor plans
